title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
note: Placeholder transcript. Run scripts/generate_transcripts.py for accurate timestamps.

chunks.text: The book opens with an invocation to the Muse and introduces the hero's situation after the fall of Troy.
This section describes the assembly of the gods and their discussion about the hero's fate.
The narrative shifts to events at the hero's home and the challenges faced by his household.
This section opens with preparations for an important assembly among the people.
The assembly convenes and various speakers address the gathered crowd about pressing matters.
The chapter concludes with preparations for a voyage and divine assistance.
The narrative follows characters arriving at a new location and witnessing religious ceremonies.
This section describes hospitality customs and conversations about past events.
Stories are shared about what happened after the great war ended.
The chapter opens with arrival at a grand palace during a celebration.
This section contains stories about adventures in distant lands and encounters with supernatural beings.
The narrative shifts back to events at home and plots being hatched by antagonists.
The gods convene again to discuss the hero's prolonged absence from home.
This section describes the hero's situation on a remote island and his longing for home.
The hero constructs a vessel and sets out to sea, facing natural challenges.
The hero arrives at a new land after surviving a storm at sea.
This section describes an encounter with a young princess and her attendants.
The hero receives guidance on how to approach the local palace and seek help.
The hero makes his way to the palace and marvels at its splendor.
This section describes the reception by the king and queen and the hero's initial appeal for assistance.
The chapter opens with preparations for athletic games and festivities.
This section includes performances by a bard singing tales of heroes and gods.
The hero demonstrates his abilities and earns the admiration of his hosts.
The hero begins recounting his adventures, starting with early encounters after leaving Troy.
This section describes the famous encounter with a one-eyed giant and the clever escape.
The hero reveals his identity to his foe, leading to a curse that will haunt his journey.
The narrative continues with the hero's visit to the keeper of the winds.
This section describes encounters with hostile peoples and significant losses among the crew.
The hero and his men arrive at an island ruled by a powerful sorceress.
The hero performs rituals to summon spirits of the dead at a sacred location.
This section describes conversations with departed souls who share prophecies and memories.
The hero encounters famous figures from the past and learns of events that occurred during his absence.
The hero receives warnings about dangers that lie ahead on his voyage.
This section describes the passage past creatures who lure sailors to their doom with song.
The crew faces additional perils and tragedy strikes when divine warnings are ignored.
The hero's tale concludes and his hosts provide gifts and transport.
This section describes the hero's arrival on his home island after years of wandering.
A goddess appears in disguise and helps the hero plan his return to his household.
The hero, disguised as a beggar, seeks shelter with a loyal servant.
This section describes the humble hospitality offered and stories shared by the fire.
The hero tests his host's loyalty by telling invented tales about himself.
The narrative shifts to the hero's son, who is prompted to return home.
This section describes the young man's departure and his journey back.
The loyal servant shares his own history while awaiting important arrivals.
Father and son are reunited in an emotional scene of recognition.
This section describes the planning of revenge against those who have wronged the household.
The antagonists learn of developments and make their own counter-plans.
The hero approaches his own home in disguise for the first time in many years.
This section describes poignant encounters including a moment with an aged and faithful animal.
The hero enters his hall and faces insults and abuse from the arrogant antagonists.
A confrontation occurs between the disguised hero and another beggar.
This section describes continued tensions in the hall and warnings given to the antagonists.
The hero has a private conversation with his wife, still maintaining his disguise.
This section describes an old servant nearly recognizing the hero through a distinctive mark.
Dreams are interpreted and a contest is proposed that will decide the future.
The hero spends a restless night contemplating the challenges ahead.
This section describes omens and preparations as the day of reckoning approaches.
The contest is announced and the famous weapon is brought forth.
This section describes the antagonists attempting and failing the challenge.
The disguised hero requests a turn and succeeds where all others failed.
The hero reveals his true identity and begins exacting justice.
This section describes the fierce battle in the hall as the antagonists are overcome.
The household is cleansed and disloyal servants face consequences.
News of the hero's return is brought to his wife, who remains cautious.
This section describes the final test by which the wife confirms her husband's identity.
The reunited couple shares stories of their experiences during the long separation.
The narrative follows the spirits of the fallen antagonists to the underworld.
This section describes the hero's reunion with his aged father.
Conflict threatens but divine intervention brings peace and the epic concludes.
